messages.author: f1c69ac31c9b9115
messages.subject: Error in geom_raster
parts:
I have a table with 12000 measurements of three variables: x, y and density.  Reading the table in:

    > d <- read.table('density.txt', header = T)
    > sum(is.na(d))
     [1] 0

so we should be good to go.  However:

    > qplot(x, y, data = d, fill = density, geom = "raster")
     Error in matrix(NA_character_, nrow = nrow, ncol = ncol) :
       invalid 'nrow' value (too large or NA)
     In addition: Warning messages:
     1: In get(x, envir = this, inherits = inh)(this, ...) :
       NAs introduced by coercion
     2: In get(x, envir = this, inherits = inh)(this, ...) :
       NAs introduced by coercion

what am I doing wrong?  Doing qplot(x, y, colour = density) works fine (although it isn't what I want).  I am running R 3.0.1 on Mac OS X with a fully up to date set of packages from CRAN.

Regards, Freddie.

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Error in geom_raster
parts:
I just made up a dataset that was 12000 rows long and it threw the same error. If you look at the example on the geom_raster() page, it lays out a grid using the pp() function. The data I made up (below) was just random data pulled from a distribution and this didn't work with the same error. 

You can use geom_point() if you change fill to color/colour=density. You can use stat_bin2d() by removing density and letting it compute density itself, but geom_raster doesn't work without some grid of X and Y values. 

d<-data.frame(x=rnorm(12000, mean=100, sd=15), y=rnorm(12000, mean=50, sd=35), density=rnorm(12000, mean=0, sd=1))

qplot(x, y, data=d, fill=density, geom="raster")
Error in matrix(NA_character_, nrow = nrow, ncol = ncol) :  vector is too large

ggplot(data=d, aes(x=x, y=y, color=density))+geom_point()
ggplot(data=d, aes(x=x, y=y))+stat_bin2d()


What exactly are you trying to get it to do? 

Brandon
